title: The same sorting in Instruction List
summary: Write the colour-sorting logic as an instruction list: one current result, labels and jumps, and two timers called with CAL.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Turn the states of a sorting sequence into compare-and-jump blocks.
Call a TON from Instruction List with CAL and read its Q output.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/ColourSeparation.il, each workpiece waits at the blade until it has lain still, then a red one is pushed onto the side belt and the plate pulled back, while a blue one is released and the blade holds the next workpiece as before.
stages.checkpoint: The program sorts the same eight workpieces as in Structured Text: red ones into RedBin, blue ones into BlueBin, then Done.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, write the four states on paper and, for each, the condition that leaves it. A JMPCN skips its block when the current result is FALSE: which result does each block test?
stages.checkpoint: Every block ends with the current result decided by State and one input; no block changes State unless its own condition holds.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter only latches Start and runs the infeed belt, so no workpiece is read or sorted. The program must sort the eight workpieces, red ones into RedBin and blue ones into BlueBin, then light Done.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press Run (F5) and open the 3D view.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named colour-separation and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the 3D view and the trace: State is not an output, so follow Hold and Push. A red workpiece keeps Push TRUE until Extended; a blue one never sets Push, and Hold is FALSE while it is let go.
stages.checkpoint: The outputs are the same as with the Structured Text solution, scan for scan, because both express the same four states.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The grade checks the bins, the lamps and that nothing was dropped; it does not read how the program is written, so the same behaviour in another language passes.
stages.checkpoint: What the assertions check is tested; nothing else is.

hints.text: Think through the sorting one situation at a time: what must be true for the program to act, and what it must write so that the next scan acts differently. Put the labels at the start of a line.

Take the states of the Structured Text sorter one at a time: each one becomes one block that ends at a label of its own. Put the labels at the start of a line. A block looks like: LD State, EQ 1, AND Extended, JMPCN next, LD 2, ST State, then the label next:. Gate the timers: LD State, EQ 0, AND Waiting, ST Gate, CAL Settle(IN := Gate, PT := T#300ms). Read the result with AND Settle.Q. Write each state as a block: LD State, EQ n, AND the condition that leaves it, JMPCN to the next block, then the instructions that change State; CAL takes variables, so store a condition in Gate before it. The states, each with its exit condition and next state: 0 wait, while Active and after Settle.Q (Settle runs while State is 0 and Waiting, PT := T#300ms), to 1 when IsRed, otherwise to 3; 1 push, to 2 when Extended; 2 retract, when Retracted add 1 to Handled and go to 0; 3 release, after Clear.Q (Clear runs while State is 3 and NOT Waiting, PT := T#1500ms, a choice and not a requirement), add 1 to Handled and go to 0. Outputs: RunIn, RunOut and RunSide follow Active; Hold is State NE 3 AND Active; Push is State EQ 1; Done is Handled GE 8; Busy is Active ANDN Done.

faultCases: The starter only latches Start and runs the infeed belt, so no workpiece is read or sorted.
